 Special election schedule set for South Carolina Senate District 31 
 By WMBF News Staff Published : Nov. 17, 2026 at 2:56 PM EST | Updated : 2 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google COLUMBIA, SC (WMBF) - A special election has been scheduled to fill the South Carolina Senate District 31 seat after Lt. Gov.-elect Mike Reichenbach’s resignation.
 Reichenbach, who currently represents Senate District 31 in Florence County, said he will resign from the Senate effective Jan. 13, 2027, as he prepares to become South Carolina’s lieutenant governor.
 SC lieutenant governor-elect shares how foster care and adoption shaped his priorities (WIS) The South Carolina Senate officially set the special-election schedule through a Writ of Election, a formal order establishing the election dates, according to the South Carolina Election Commission.
 Reichenbach was elected in a March 2022 special election to fill the unexpired term of the late Sen. Hugh K. Leatherman Sr.
 Election schedule 
 Candidate filing: Noon Dec. 4 through noon Dec. 11, 2026 
 Primary election: Jan. 26, 2027 
 Primary runoff, if needed: Feb. 9, 2027 
 Special election: April 6, 2027 
 Early voting 
 Early voting for the primary will run from Jan. 11 through Jan. 22, from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Early voting locations will be closed on Martin Luther King Jr. Day and weekends.
 If a primary runoff is needed, early voting will be held Feb. 3-5.
 Early voting for the special election will run from March 22 through April 2, from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. There will be no Saturday or Sunday early voting.
 The Election Commission said the primary must be held on the first eligible election date on or after the 11th Tuesday following the vacancy.
